items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: So I got a job with Lucky Millinder. Lucky Millinder had a very good band, a great band. However, I stayed there, I think it was three weeks and I got fired

ctx.x: Yes, I knew John Kirby. John Kirby, why, I first saw him with Fletcher's band in 1930 down in Cincinnati, he had his tuba and his bass fiddle. Now, he was the first tuba player I heard play a lip vibrato on the tuba, and it was pretty. It was pretty, although he didn't play tuba too much after Fletcher's band. I don't know -- when he went with Lucky Millinder, he left Fletcher and went with Lucky, I don't know whether he played too much tuba then.
Well, the tuba was beginning to fade out.
